title: Centripetal force; Electric field strength and field lines
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: C02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; F03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; C02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; F03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C02-1#N.3a, F03-1#N.2, C02-1#N.4a, F03-1#N.11, C02-1#N.15.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Friction
items.clue: On a flat bend, the only sideways push on a car from the road.

items.label: Neutral point
items.clue: Place between two like charges where E = 0, nearer the smaller one.

items.label: Tangent
items.clue: Straight line along which a whirled ball flies off if its string is cut.

items.label: Electric field
items.clue: Region where a charge feels a force, present even with nothing placed in it.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides around a flat circular track at a constant speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about her motion is correct?

options.text: Her velocity is constant, so the resultant force acting on her is zero.
Her velocity changes, so a resultant force acts towards the centre.
A resultant force acts on her outwards, away from the centre of the track.
A resultant force acts on her forwards, along her direction of motion.

questions.stem: At point P, a charge of +2.0 µC experiences an electric force of 5.0 × 10⁻³ N directed east. This charge is removed and a charge of −6.0 µC is placed at P; the charges that produce the field do not move. Taking east as positive, what is the electric force on the −6.0 µC charge?

A car travels at constant speed around a bend on a flat horizontal road; its path is part of a horizontal circle. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the horizontal forces on the car is correct?

options.text: Friction from the road acts towards the centre and is the resultant force.
Friction acts towards the centre and is balanced by a centrifugal force.
Friction and a separate centripetal force both act towards the centre.
A forward driving force along the bend is the resultant force on the car.

questions.stem: The field lines of a long, straight charged wire spread out radially, in planes at right angles to the wire: they spread in two dimensions, not three. Point P is 2.0 cm from the wire and point Q is 6.0 cm from it, both far from the wire's ends. How does the electric field strength at P compare with that at Q?

options.text: E at P is 9 times E at Q, as the field strength falls with the square of the distance.
E at P is 3 times E at Q, as the same lines spread over 3 times the area at Q.
E is the same at P and Q, as every line that passes P also passes Q.
E at Q is 3 times E at P, as the larger cylinder at Q holds more lines.

questions.stem: A car drives at constant speed over the top of a rounded hill in the road. Near the top, the road's vertical cross-section is a circular arc. The car stays in contact with the road. At the top, how does the normal force from the road compare with the car's weight?

options.text: It equals the weight, since at the top the car moves neither up nor down.
It is greater than the weight, as when the car drives through a dip.
It is less than the weight, so the forces on it add to a downward force.
It equals the weight plus mv²/r, to balance an outward force.

questions.explanation: The centre of the arc is below the car, so the forces must add up to mv²/r downwards: weight − normal force = mv²/r. The normal force is less than the weight by mv²/r.
